faq.q: What is the origin of Yasmine?

No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Yasmine can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Yasmine, yasmine. Script forms are يَاسَمِين, یاسمن, یاسمین, यासमीन.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
